steps.note: S1.2.1 states the net target change (JV+RG)x is independent of the initial side and central values a, c, with rows 0-1 subtracting, rows 2-5 adding and rows 6-7 restoring c, a, matching the paper.
S1.2.2 gives central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, side wires cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, zero/two-point triples already zero, and self coefficient one.
S1.2.3 gives central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2, side term cancelling distinct triples meeting in zero or two points, intersection one contributing zero, self coefficient one.
S1.2.4 gives the three stages (x,y) -> (x,y+x) -> (-y,y+x) -> (-y,x); S1.2 and S1.2.1 state each invocation restores its scratch wires.

The plan gives only the general rule (S1.4.1 method: edge rank is the residual dimension) and the 'comparable labels' claim in S1.4.1.5, but never lists the per-edge orthogonal residuals and their dimensions (the residual table).

S1.4.1.4 states the inclusion <t_X> in t_Y-perp because t_X is orthogonal to t_Y (in the label construction), but not the complement <t_X,t_Y>-perp of dimension h-2 that the residual of side edge 2 to 5 needs.
The plan states sources N and sinks Wm-N (S1.4.1.2), the only decreasing edge centre 3 to 4 losing h (S1.4.1.5), telescoping to signed Wm-2N (S1.4.1.6) and L=Ich giving absolute Wm-2N+2L (S1.4.1.7).
S1.4.1.7b says each nonzero residual is nondegenerate with a norm-one unit (nonalternating), hence has an orthonormal basis, and alternating planes are absorbed by replacing w with w+a, w+b, w+a+b.
S1.4.1.7c states L_b/N = 100/539 and L_c/N = 101/539, both below 1/2.

S1.4.1.9.2 gives weight additivity mod 4 on orthogonal binary vectors (via the intersection-parity formula), and S1.4.1.9 method/motivation say the phase difference of nested labels splits over an orthonormal residual basis into one phase per vector; the explicit sum formula is not written but the content is stated.
S1.4.1.9.3 states wt(v) odd, coefficient +-1 mod 4, the identity i^(eps[v.x]) = (1+i^eps)/2 + (1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^(v.x), and H diag(1,-1) H = X turning it into aI+bX_v or its inverse.
The plan counts one kernel per residual vector and s_c in total (S1.4.1.9, S1.4.1.9.4) but never states the tensoring over k columns (each residual vector giving one factor acting on all k columns).

S1.4.4.1.9 only restates the proposition (C tensor m on every role) and mentions 27 inverse factors fixed by C = iZC^-1Z; it omits the endpoint frames (zero label I, full label C tensor m), the supp(u_a) derivation, the specific Z before and i^(27k)Z after repair, and the explicit negation of X outputs.
The plan states both loss ratios are below 1/2 and that the deficit N-2L_b (resp. 2N-2L_c) is positive, giving s_b < W_b m and s_c < W_c m.
S1.4.2.1 gives eta_b = 339/22587335000000, matching the paper.
S1.4.2.1 gives eta_c = 73/19906842167500, matching the paper.
The plan states both deficits exceed 20*2^-50, log m < 20, m^(1-2^-50) > m(1-20*2^-50) > m(1-eta), hence s/W < m^tau with tau = sigma = 1-2^-50.

S1.4.3.1.2 gives the elimination (topmost nonzero row, rightmost pivot, clear by lower-triangular operations, delete row and column, repeat on the active indices, each step a rank-one block) and S1.4.3.1.1 gives Pi with exactly a ones.

S1.4.3.1.3 says a prime q avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators is used (shear over Z/q^b, diagonal units), which is the paper's prime choice, though stated compactly without the 'finite table' wording.
S1.4.3.1.3 states a lower triangular transformation costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order, each by a diagonal unit and a fixed combination of earlier coordinates.
S1.4.3.1.4 gives D_j += H_i, interchange, D_j = H_i - D_j taking (h,d) to (h+d,d), and S1.4.3.1.5 states one interchange per one of Pi, a in all.

The plan defines E = 64(W+m+1)^3, B = s+E, C_1 = max{20,nu+3} = 20 and Delta = ceil(C_0 d^C_1), but never defines C_0 = 128 m B^2 (only 'bounded by 128mB^2 d^(nu+3) <= C_0 d^C_1'), nor nu as the least j with m^j >= B, nor nu = 11.

S1.4.4.4.1 states A(e) <= sA(e/m)+E at an internal node and A(e) <= 8e at a leaf, with E bounding the per-invocation scalar gates (24W^3), child corrections (4s) and bank corrections; S1.4.4.4.2 explains why s and not s/W.
The plan gives sx+E <= Bx, B^(k+1) <= B^2 d^nu, A(e) <= 8B^2 d^(nu+1), and the total below 128 m B^2 d^(nu+3) <= C_0 d^C_1 with C_1 = 20.
S1.4.4.4.6 gives values in 2^-(p+l)Z[i] with modulus at most 2^l by induction, exact with p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits; S1.4.4.4.7 gives eps*C_1 < 1 so Delta = o(p).
S1.4.4.5.3 states every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disk arrays map to disk arrays, and componentwise truncation preserves the disk with error below sqrt2 * 2^-p.

summary: 21 of 26 sub-steps present. Absent: L1 (no per-edge residual table with dimensions), L2 (inclusion stated but not the h-2 complement), P3 (no k-column tensoring of residual factors), P4 (endpoint frames and Z/phase repair not derived, only the proposition restated), S1 (C_0 and nu never defined). The bank-exchange network (B1-B4), rank-saving (R1-R4), matrix-shear (M1-M4) and most of simultaneous-layer (S2-S5) are carried out in full.
